description:
Redwood Inference is entering Q1 2026 with increased focus on predictable serving latency/throughput across regions, GPU SKUs, and top customer traffic shapes. The “Perf baseline & representative workload suite” project establishes a repeatable, CI-backed benchmarking program that produces a Q1 2026 baseline for the serving runtime (kernel + scheduling) and a representative workload suite that can be used for regression detection, release signoff, and model-catalog performance profiles.

Goals:
- Define and publish Q1 2026 “golden” latency/throughput baselines for Redwood’s top deployed models (e.g., Llama-family, Qwen-family, Mistral-family variants) across key hardware (H100/A100/L40S where applicable) and regions (at least us-east and eu-west).
- Build a representative workload suite that mirrors production traffic shapes: chat streaming (short prompts, variable decode), long-context summarization (large prefill), tool/function calling (bursty multi-turn), and embeddings (high-QPS small payload).
- Make results reproducible and attributable: strict environment capture (driver/runtime version, kernel selection, scheduling policy, batch/caching configs), workload seeds, and run manifests.
- Integrate the suite into automated canaries and release gating (perf-canary + CI), with clearly defined thresholds for “regression” vs “noise,” plus escalation/triage playbooks.

Scope:
- Serving runtime internals: scheduler policies (continuous batching heuristics, backpressure, queueing disciplines), KV cache management, prefill/decode overlap, kernel auto-selection, and instrumentation required to explain tail latency.
- Benchmarking infrastructure: harness, workload generators, run orchestration, results storage formats, and dashboards.
- Cross-functional alignment: Applied ML/Evals ensures workload representativeness and model-variant comparability; SRE/Observability ensures production-aligned metrics and alerting.

Out of scope (for this phase):
- New model onboarding work beyond what is required to include top models in the suite.
- Customer-facing marketing benchmarks; the deliverable is internal baselines first, with optional downstream publication.

Stakeholders & roles:
- Primary engineering owners: Mateo Alvarez (runtime org lead), Hiro Tanaka (kernels), Sofia Ivanova (scheduling), Noah Patel (runtime architecture).
- Benchmarking owners: Rina Kobayashi (perf benchmarks), Claire Dubois (methodology), Jonas Weber (perf/evals program).
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Aisha Bello, Sergio Costa (dashboards + alerting + gating hygiene).
- Exec sponsors: Neha Kapoor (infra/reliability), Dr. Maya Srinivasan (applied ML).

Timeline (Q1 2026):
- Late Q4 2025: agree on workload taxonomy + methodology; implement harness primitives; wire up basic dashboards.
- Early Q1 2026: run baseline sweeps for top models/regions; validate noise model; calibrate regression thresholds.
- Mid Q1 2026: integrate canary + CI gating; publish runbooks; start using results in runtime release signoff.
- Late Q1 2026: finalize baseline report and “v1” representative suite; create backlog for v2 workloads and additional hardware/regions.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence: methodology + baseline report + ADRs for measurement choices; runbooks for reruns/triage.
- GitHub: benchmark harness + workload suite + scheduler/kernel instrumentation + perf-canary integration.
- Linear: execution plan broken into workstreams with dependencies and acceptance criteria.
- Slack: coordination, rapid triage, scheduling, and decision-making threads.
- Google Drive: working drafts, spreadsheets of baseline runs, and scratchpads used during calibration.
- Jira: a small number of support/ops tickets when baseline work uncovers production issues or access problems.
- Gmail/Fireflies (limited): leadership/partner coordination on benchmarking environments and any external technical deep-dive needed for hardware/driver guidance.

files.description: Published plan for Q1 2026 baselines: models/hardware/regions matrix, workload taxonomy, required metrics (p50/p95/p99 TTFT, TPOT, throughput), and success criteria; includes ownership and weekly cadence.
Definition of the v1 representative workload suite: workload shapes, request mixes, sequence-length distributions, streaming vs non-streaming modes, and how each maps to production cohorts.
Scheduler configuration baseline (knobs, defaults, guardrails) used for Q1 2026 runs; rationale for queue discipline, backpressure thresholds, fairness policy, and overload behavior.
Kernel auto-selection rules and expected fallbacks by model family and sequence length; notes on known performance cliffs and required driver/CUDA/Triton constraints.
Step-by-step profiling playbook for reproducing perf results: how to capture traces, kernel timelines, scheduler logs, and how to label runs for later comparison.
Company-wide standard for perf regressions: noise model, minimum sample sizes, pass/fail thresholds, and how perf gating ties into runtime release processes.
ADR documenting canonical perf metrics (TTFT/TPOT/throughput) and the run-manifest schema (env capture, model config, scheduler config, workload seed) used across tools.
ADR describing how the workload suite is derived from production telemetry (histograms/cohorts) while avoiding sensitive prompt content; includes privacy constraints and sampling approach.
Mapping between SLO dashboards and baseline metrics: which SLO views correspond to baseline cohorts, and how baseline changes should (or should not) affect SLO alerting.
Dashboard spec for baseline reporting (Grafana/Looker-style): panels for TTFT/TPOT percentiles, throughput, saturation indicators, and links to run manifests and traces.
Working notes and open questions: candidate workloads, initial run results, suspected noise sources, and TODOs before freezing the baseline.
Spreadsheet-style tracker of baseline runs: model, region, GPU SKU, runtime build, scheduler config, sample size, and links to artifacts; includes conditional formatting for regressions.
Table of request-mix definitions (percent weights per workload) and their parameters (prompt length bins, output length bins, concurrency targets).
Scratchpad capturing variance investigations (GPU clock variability, container placement, NUMA, warmup, cache effects) with hypotheses and quick experiments.
Draft metrics dictionary for perf suite runs: metric names, units, aggregation rules, and tagging conventions for model/workload/region/hardware.
Applied ML memo on ensuring perf baselines don’t unintentionally change decoding behavior/quality; includes minimal quality spot-check plan and prompts/eval references.
Draft proposal for integrating perf gating into runtime releases: which jobs run on PR vs nightly, gating exceptions, and escalation paths.
Capacity plan for benchmark fleet: GPU-hours by SKU, scheduling windows, expected contention, and cost estimates; includes assumptions and risk register.
Umbrella execution ticket: scope definition, milestone checklist, and links to methodology docs; includes sub-issues for harness, workloads, dashboards, and gating.
Implement standardized manifest/results schema (per ADR-0172) across benchmark tools; acceptance includes versioning and backwards compatibility.
Define and implement chat streaming workload generator with realistic concurrency, prompt-length distribution, and streaming cadence; includes validation vs prod telemetry.
Work item for long-context summarization workload (large prefill, modest decode) including KV cache pressure and prefill latency measurement.
Embeddings workload definition and harness support (high QPS, small payloads) with throughput and tail latency reporting.
Add scheduler instrumentation: queue wait time, batch assembly time, batch size distributions, drop/load-shed counters, and correlation IDs for traces.
Expose kernel choice decisions per run (or sampled): selected kernel, fallback reason, and sequence-length regime; used to explain performance deltas.
Integrate representative suite into perf-canary; define regression thresholds and notification routing; includes dry-run period and tuning.
Create baseline dashboards and drill-down links to manifests/traces; includes role-based views for runtime vs SRE.
PM ticket to package the baseline report for internal stakeholders (execs, product, sales engineering): summary tables, takeaways, and rollout gating policy.
PR adding the canonical run manifest JSON schema, validator, and example manifests; includes CI checks to prevent schema drift.
PR implementing chat streaming workload generator (request mix, concurrency ramp, streaming token pacing) and producing baseline metrics (TTFT/TPOT) output.
PR adding long-context workload plus standardized warmup procedure to reduce variance; includes docs and example runs.
PR adding embeddings mode with throughput-first reporting (req/s, tokens/s where applicable) and percentile latency export.
Runtime PR adding scheduler metrics for queue wait, batch assembly, and batch size distribution; includes guardrails to limit overhead in prod.
Runtime PR adding optional kernel selection dumps tagged to benchmark runs; helps attribute regressions to kernel auto-selection changes.
PR adjusting scheduling/backpressure defaults to reduce p99 TTFT on long-prefill workloads while protecting throughput; includes before/after baseline comparisons.
PR wiring representative suite into nightly canary runs and adding a gating mode for release branches; includes threshold config and reporting.
PR adding dashboards/alerts for baseline runs: TTFT/TPOT percentiles, throughput, and variance panels; integrates links to run manifests.
PR adding optional quality spot-check hooks (prompt set sampling, basic output sanity checks) to ensure perf changes don’t break decoding behavior.
Thread coordinating kickoff logistics: owners, initial scope, and where to store baseline run artifacts; includes links to Linear umbrella ticket.
Thread debating canonical metrics definitions (TTFT vs first-token-on-wire, TPOT with/without client overhead) and agreeing on measurement boundaries.
Thread reviewing ADR-0172 draft: schema fields, versioning, and how to handle workload parameters and environment capture.
Thread with Applied ML/Evals validating workload representativeness vs telemetry; discusses sequence length bins and request-mix weights.
Thread on benchmark fleet stability and variance sources (GPU clocks, placement); SRE proposes standard warmup and isolation steps.
Thread triaging a surprising p99 regression on long-prefill workloads; includes quick profiler screenshots, kernel selection suspects, and next steps.
Thread coordinating scheduler instrumentation details (new counters, tags) and confirming overhead expectations and sampling strategy.
Thread aligning on dashboard requirements and run naming conventions so engineers can drill from dashboard → manifest → traces.
Thread planning baseline sweep schedule (models x regions x SKUs) and reserving benchmark cluster windows; includes a spreadsheet link.
Thread discussing chat streaming pacing (server push vs client read) and how to avoid measuring client bottlenecks.
Thread on integrating perf-canary alerts with on-call routing; defines which alerts page vs which go to a triage channel.
Thread confirming the baseline freeze date and which runtime build/tag is considered the Q1 2026 baseline anchor.
Thread resolving disagreement about including caching in baselines (prefix/KV cache); ends with decision to report both cold and warm scenarios.
Thread where a baseline run uncovers a production-adjacent regression signature; incident bot posts a low-severity alert and team decides it’s a canary-only issue.
Thread coordinating PR reviews for scheduler metrics and manifest validator; includes requested changes and CI rerun notes.
Thread confirming minimal quality spot-check prompts for perf runs and agreeing on a small “must-not-break” set.
Thread about benchmark cluster permissions and service accounts; leads to an internal Jira helpdesk ticket.
Thread summarizing first full sweep results (high-level numbers) and highlighting the biggest variance drivers; points to Drive tracker.
Thread discussing kernel fallback behavior on one SKU and deciding to pin a kernel for baseline runs until auto-selection is fixed.
Customer support ticket opened after baseline work correlates with a real customer report: includes environment, affected models, dashboards, mitigation, and references to related PRs.
Internal helpdesk ticket to fix benchmark fleet IAM/permissions for running GPU jobs and exporting artifacts; includes root cause and resolution.

Email thread in Ava Chen’s mailbox sharing an exec readout: baseline status, risks (variance, fleet capacity), and asks for prioritization/support; internal participants limited to leadership/manager set.
Email thread in Neha Kapoor’s mailbox approving benchmark fleet reservations and GPU-hour budget; includes attachment stubs for the capacity plan sheet.
Technical deep dive transcript with a hardware partner on benchmarking stability (driver/CUDA settings, clock locking, isolation); ends with action items and recommended settings for baseline runs.
